newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar trades tight range to end little-changed.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar trades tight range to end little-changed.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed on Tuesday, with offshore selling capping any attempted rallies.
The currency ended at US$0.7034/41 and 68.05 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7032/39 and 67.98 at the opening.
A Wellington dealer said there was reasonable interest to buy in the low 0.7030s, with some rumours of more samurai business to be done.
He saw the kiwi in range-trade mode at the moment and likely to move between 0.7025-50 overnight.
An Auckland dealer was more bearish, saying key support at 0.7030 appeared vulnerable and the currency could test lower towards 0.70 cents.

The market is gearing up for December quarter inflation data on Friday, with debt market traders predicting further interest rate falls if underlying inflation comes in below the Reserve Bank's forecast of 0.5 percent, for an annual 2.3 percent.

The dealer said his bearishness was based on a combination of factors: possible rate falls post-CPI, a "toppy" TWI, the possibility that politicians may try to talk down the currency when they return from their summer break, and the relative scarcity of samurai interest compared with last year.
